The added diagnostic closed the worker-flush, real-tensor export, score-only IVF and detailed scheduler/JSON measurement gaps. This is one observer-on attribution run, not another product comparison. Original five product point estimates and all eight-arm artifacts remain unchanged.

All45 requests completed with exact input/output token lists and ordered native key bytes matching product ARC;3264 output tokens in40.218s. CPU validation266passed with CUDA initialization forbidden. Model lifecycle73.453s including postload export/replay; GPU busy time was not measured. Explicit postload RPC8110.375ms, of which the first index build dominated. No product arm rerun, model download/build, pool/admission change or synthetic expansion.

Main worker+engine load-only source and runtime snapshots were saved explicitly before teardown, after all45 completions. Full scheduler/model-runner summaries now exist, with dropped records0. Initial eight-arm worker snapshots remain partial and have not been retroactively completed.

The capture index-upload boundary wraps the real `torch.tensor(last_indices,device=GPU)` call. Its13.217s host/13.221s threadCPU can include implicit waiting/spinning for prior GPU work;72 stream samples total only4.262ms and are not all1139 calls. Gathering and reduction are much smaller observed host ranges. Neither these inclusive ranges nor the model runner can be added to estimate additional compute or reclaimable latency. GPU event intervals can include idle host launch gaps; no CUPTI/kernel-only or isolated DMA duration claim. The diagnostic used the root-provided profiling-only split; query algorithms and measured production source are unchanged.

Actual clock/queue boundaries: complete runtime summaries contain scheduler.schedule1175calls/167.005ms wall/153.437ms threadCPU, scheduler.update1175calls/91.938ms wall, and45 scheduler.add_request observations. scheduler-queue.csv contains each add-return→first-schedule waiting envelope, first-schedule→actual worker prepare-host and prepare-host→client first-token. Host prepare is not device-ready/first-kernel completion. API and worker queues/transport remain separate inclusive envelopes, not a residual arithmetic estimate.

First index build8.081s wall/7.973s threadCPU and8.081s stream range is a COLD first-use observation. It may include library/kernel initialization or host launch delays, not8s pure GPU math; no warmed rebuild was measured or inferred, and no warmup/repetition was added. Even excluding build, observed small-pool indexed route/gather/exact/readback spans exceed flat math/readback, with extra per-query calls. This is no index win for the11-row diagnostic; large-pool crossover remains unmeasured. Live GPU allocated bytes changed214016 bytes during replay; that is an end-state delta, not a measured peak or reduced model/KV allocation. No GPU pool or DRAM inflation.

Counter-label correction: original export.json main_profile_pending_after_fence=2 was populated later, after replay created two root-profiler search event pairs. The explicit assert and immutable load-only snapshot establish0 immediately after the main fence; final root profiler drained0. Raw result is preserved, with this correction in evidence/analysis.json. This is not two unready main-workload events.

Remaining limits: isolated DMA-private-stream device time, pure transport/network time, Python-object index memory peak, independently attributed cold-build initialization, and warmed/large-pool crossover are unmeasured. No production, significance, capacity, direct-adoption or broad semantic-value claim. All natural consumed prefixes in this trace still use the real partial-prefix splice fallback.
